Brand: The Ardmore Hotel

The Ardmore is a 42-room independent hotel in the Scottish Highlands. Positioned as "off-grid luxury" — no conference rooms, no spa, no pool, just extraordinary landscape, exceptional food, and deliberate disconnection. Price: £380–£580 per night for double occupancy.

Campaign: Drive winter bookings (November–February), a traditionally soft season. Target couples aged 35–55 who are considering an anniversary stay, a significant birthday, or a "reset" trip.

Objectives: Fill 65% of available winter nights (current rate: 48%), grow direct booking share to reduce OTA dependency (currently 60% OTA), build email list of high-intent future guests.

Budget: £18,000.

Timeline: Campaign starts late October. Needs to convert bookings for November through February window.

Channels: Instagram (visual storytelling), email (direct to existing inquirers and past guests), Meta paid targeting, PR/editorial outreach to one travel publication.

Audience: Couples 35–55, household income £100k+, UK-based (primarily London, Edinburgh, Manchester). They have been to luxury hotels but feel they are getting "the same thing everywhere." They want something that feels genuinely different, not just expensive. Sensitivities: "curated" language that feels manufactured, anything that sounds like a wellness retreat, stock photography of fireplaces and tartan.

Constraints: No "escape" or "disconnect" as the main hook — overused in the category. No manufactured testimonials or fabricated guest stories. Winter photography must be authentic to the property — no stock. No price guarantees or "best rate" claims.

Open questions: Whether to involve a known travel writer for a hosted stay, whether to run a winter package vs promote room-only.
